channel.title: Start Investing Simple
channel.description: Plain-English guides to investing, saving, and money basics for beginners.

item.title: Sinking Funds: How to Save for Predictable Big Expenses Without Debt
item.description: Learn what a sinking fund is, how it differs from an emergency fund, and how to use one to pay for expected big expenses without going into debt.

item.title: Understanding Market Volatility: Why Staying Invested Matters
item.description: Learn why stock markets fluctuate, why volatility isn't the same as losing money, and why staying invested through downturns has historically mattered more than timing them.

item.title: Social Security Basics: What to Know Before You Retire
item.description: A plain-English overview of how Social Security retirement benefits work, how your benefit amount is calculated, and how claiming age affects your monthly payment.

item.title: The HSA: A Health Savings Account That Doubles as a Retirement Tool
item.description: Learn how Health Savings Accounts work, their unique triple tax advantage, and why some people use them as an extra retirement savings vehicle.

item.title: High-Yield Savings Accounts Explained: Why Your Emergency Fund Deserves One
item.description: Learn how high-yield savings accounts work, how they differ from regular savings accounts, and what to check before opening one.

item.title: Understanding Credit Scores: What They Are and Why They Matter
item.description: Learn what a credit score actually measures, what factors influence it, and practical habits for building or improving it over time.

item.title: Budgeting Methods That Actually Work: Finding One You'll Stick With
item.description: Compare popular budgeting methods — zero-based budgeting, the envelope method, and pay-yourself-first — to find the approach that fits your habits.

item.title: What Are Dividends and How Do They Work?
item.description: A plain-English explanation of stock dividends, how dividend payments work, and what dividend reinvestment means for long-term investors.

item.title: Understanding Risk Tolerance and Asset Allocation
item.description: Learn what risk tolerance means, how it shapes your investment mix, and how to think about your own comfort with market ups and downs.

item.title: What Is an ETF? Exchange-Traded Funds Explained Simply
item.description: Learn what ETFs are, how they differ from mutual funds, and why they've become one of the most popular ways for beginners to invest.

item.title: How Much Do You Actually Need to Retire?
item.description: A beginner-friendly look at common frameworks for estimating retirement savings needs, including the 4% rule, and why the honest answer is 'it depends.'

item.title: Debt Snowball vs. Debt Avalanche: Which Payoff Method Is Right for You?
item.description: Compare the debt snowball and debt avalanche methods for paying off multiple debts, including the math behind each and which one tends to work better for different people.

item.title: The 50/30/20 Budget Rule: A Simple Starting Point for Managing Your Money
item.description: Learn how the 50/30/20 budgeting rule works, how to apply it to your own income, and where it falls short for some people.

item.title: What Is a 401(k) and How Does It Actually Work?
item.description: A plain-English guide to how 401(k) retirement plans work, what employer matching means, and why they're one of the most valuable benefits many workers have access to.

item.title: Stocks vs. Bonds: Understanding the Basic Building Blocks of Investing
item.description: A beginner's guide to how stocks and bonds work, how their risk and return differ, and why most portfolios include a mix of both.

item.title: What Is Dollar-Cost Averaging? A Simple Strategy for Nervous Investors
item.description: Learn how dollar-cost averaging works, why it helps reduce the stress of market timing, and how it compares to investing a lump sum all at once.

item.title: Roth IRA vs. Traditional IRA: Which One Should You Choose?
item.description: A plain-English breakdown of how Roth and Traditional IRAs differ in taxes, withdrawals, and eligibility — and how to decide which fits your situation.

item.title: Why You Should Build an Emergency Fund Before You Start Investing
item.description: Learn why financial experts recommend saving an emergency fund first, how much to save, and where to keep it.

item.title: Index Funds vs. Individual Stocks: Which Should Beginners Choose?
item.description: A clear comparison of index funds and individual stocks to help new investors decide where to put their first dollars.

item.title: What Is Compound Interest and Why It's Called the Eighth Wonder of the World
item.description: A plain-English explanation of how compound interest works, why time matters more than the amount you invest, and how to use it to your advantage.
